plain_description.what: Re-fits the small model that predicts when the judge goes wrong. The predictor "do the two answers agree?" is now computed from the models' extracted answers on the evaluation questions instead of from the judged questions. Uses the 12-model MMLU-Pro board, with no new judge calls.
plain_description.why: Checks whether how the agreement predictor was defined could have biased the judge-error model, and whether its main slope is actually supported by the cases where the right answer is firmly known.
plain_description.information: If nothing moves, the earlier fit holds. If the numbers shift, the predictor was biased by which questions got judged. Result: passed as a consistency check only. On this evenly spread schedule the two definitions are almost identical (correlation 0.997), so the test had no power against the bias it was meant to catch, and that bias remains untested. The slope passed its registered rule but is only borderline once questions are resampled in groups by subject. It also showed that an earlier claim that MMLU-Pro is 100% decidable by the answer key was false (0.68 to 0.98 per subject). It was later ruled history rather than evidence, because it ran on the older question pool.
